## Intent
Hypothesis: manual 4× unrolling of the branchy integrate-decide-respawn loop can amortize per-particle overhead and approach the streaming ceiling without auto-vectorization.

## Layout & approach
The AoS layout offers 68 B/particle; loop 1 touches 32 B (47% hot — age+pos+seed+vel), loop 2 touches 28 B (41% hot — color+pos); the remaining 53–59% per line is dead weight. No intermediate storage — the death verdict stays in registers. The 4× unroll processes four particles per iteration at stride 0x44 (68 B), but each particle uses scalar xmm ops, not cross-particle SIMD. With 47% hot bytes and no packing, streaming efficiency is poor — but the code never reaches the memory system hard enough for that to matter.

## Cache saturation
The ns/p is strikingly flat across all N: at q=0.01, 25.43–26.21 ns/p from L3-resident (N=10000) to DRAM (N=10000000); at q=0.5, 34.21–34.20. No spill knee appears at the L3→DRAM transition. This flatness is the signature of a frontend-bound kernel — working-set residence is irrelevant because the decode pipeline cannot feed the backend fast enough to saturate any cache level.

## Bandwidth
Achieved bandwidth is 2.0–2.67 GB/s — 16–21% of the 12.69 GB/s ceiling. The memory floor is 5.359 ns/p; this algo runs at 25–34 ns/p, 4.7–6.4× above the floor: frontend/overhead-bound, not bandwidth-bound. Frontend_stall dominates at 64–69% across all profiles; backend_stall and branch_flush are both 0.0%. Against baseline the algo is 0.98–1.01× — indistinguishable from scalar. Against the winner it is 1.8–3.3× slower; the gap narrows from 3.3× at q=0.01 to 1.97× at q=0.5 as the vectorized winner also suffers branchy respawn, but this algo never closes the gap.

## Assembly
The 791-instruction body is 4× unrolled, each copy processing one particle with scalar xmm ops: `vmovss`, `vmulss`, `vaddss` for integration; `vucomiss`+`jae` for the death check; `call Data.spawn` for branchy respawn. The PRNG uses `rorx`/`shl`/`xor`/`lzcnt`. Component-wise `vmulps`/`vaddps` operate within a single particle — no ymm/zmm, no gather. The render loop does byte-granular scatter: `movzx`+`add`+`cmp`+`cmovae`+`mov BYTE PTR` per RGBA channel. The 4×-duplicated body overwhelms the L1I/decode pipeline, directly causing the 64–69% frontend stalls.

## Verdict
Refuted — 0.98–1.01× of baseline at every N×q point: manual unrolling without cross-particle vectorization provides no benefit over scalar. The 791-instruction body drives frontend_stall to 64–69%, capping BW at 2.0–2.67 GB/s (16–21% of ceiling, 4.7–6.4× above the 5.359 ns/p floor). The winner (autovec) is 1.8–3.3× faster; the gap narrows at high q (3.3×→1.97×) only because respawn branches penalize the vectorized winner too, but this algo never approaches it.
